notes: EPISTEMIC-RACES first race runs: deepseek-v4-pro vs deepseek-v4-flash on races 1 and 2. Conductor = glm-5.2/T371 (non-deepseek; the Orcha 2026-08-05 ruling bars a competing-family conductor). RACE 2 (honest refusal, confusion matrix vs key, point iff verdict correct AND gap named correctly): both lanes 4/6. deepseek-v4-flash: promote-correct 1/3, refuse-correct 3/3 — errors were two FALSE REFUSALS of grounded packets (R2-P1, R2-P3), i.e. a blanket-skepticism lean. deepseek-v4-pro: promote-correct 2/3, refuse-correct 2/3 — errors were one false refusal (R2-P2, over-applied per-goban independence) and one WRONG-GAP refusal (R2-P4 named C-A2 deferral instead of the keyed 'no denominator'). Clocks (tools/runner trailer): pro wall 115.9s cpu 0.95s rss 195MB out 3382B exit 0 (1 attempt); flash wall 616.8s cpu 3.75s rss 216MB out 6179B exit 0 on attempt 2 — attempt 1 was wall-killed at 600.2s with 0 output and 3.26s CPU (an API/network stall: near-idle CPU over the wall = waiting, not compute). Tokens: no reading (operator-collected per protocol; tokens.template.md left for the operator). CONFOUND (headline, not footnote): the packet author is deepseek-v4-flash (recorded in MANIFEST.md) and deepseek-v4-flash is also a lane; key tampering is excluded (SHA-256 of keys + all 15 lane-facing packet files re-verified against the register committed at b7c382c before any lane ran), but a family-level prior remains — the exam's phrasing came from the same family that sits it. Therefore a Flash win does NOT license a capability claim; it licenses a replication against a packet set authored by a different family (registered as the follow-up). A Flash loss would have been the informative outcome (survives the confound). On this run Flash won race 1 (3/3 vs 2/3) and tied race 2 (4/6 vs 4/6) — confounded in Flash's favour, so it licenses only the replication, not a capability ranking. Serving-tag caveat carried forward: Flash is on a preview-channel bump reported 2026-08-05, so the label does not pin the model across dates. n=1 standing: one run per model is an anecdote, not a ranking. PROTOCOL FINDINGS (report-don't-adapt, not fixed): (1) the bakeoff harness execute() cannot run from a git worktree because find_root() requires isdir(.git) and a worktree's .git is a file — lanes were instead run via the --emit block executed from a worktree; (2) the worktree boundary is a RELATIVE-path boundary only: the harness does not pass --no-tools to pi, so a tool-using lane could in principle reach the main repo's untracked/race-keys via absolute paths; mitigated here by the inlined self-contained brief and the harness header instructing no shell commands, but this is a structural gap. Calibration (ran BEFORE any lane score was read): race-1 grader — vacuous kills neither, known-killer earns the point, near-identical twin (null control) also earns the point, wrong-seed killer earns none, for all 3 packets; race-2 residue grader (conductor glm-5.2, non-deepseek) — correct-gap verdicts ranked above wrong-gap verdicts (R2-P4/P5/P6) and two near-identical correct R2-P4 verdicts scored identically. Evidence: untracked/bakeoff/pro-vs-flash/ (out.md, trailer.log per lane, lanes.json, grading/A.md|B.md, A.scores.json|B.scores.json, prompt.txt, roster.txt); run document docs/evidence/EPISTEMIC-RACES/runs/2026-08-05-pro-vs-flash.md.
